title: tutorial
text: Many Hugging Face datasets provide predefined train, test, optionally validation splits. splits available $splits field HFData object vectors row IDs, allowing reused directly mlr3 workflows. predefined train test splits can passed directly ResamplingCustom, allowing original dataset split reused instead generating new one. resulting resampling object can used like mlr3 resampling strategy.
code: library(mlr3learners)  hf_data = hfdt(   repo_id = "a4n9i/scikit_iris",   config = "default",   target = "Species",   task_type= "classif" )  task = as_task(hf_data)  train_row_id = hf_data$splits$train test_row_id  = hf_data$splits$test resampling = rsmp("custom")  resampling$instantiate(   task,   train_sets = list(train_row_id),   test_sets = list(test_row_id) )  resampling ##  ## ── <ResamplingCustom> : Custom Splits ────────────────────────────────────────── ## • Iterations: 1 ## • Instantiated: TRUE ## • Parameters: list() rr = resample(   task,   lrn("classif.rpart"),   resampling )  rr$aggregate() ## classif.ce  ##  0.6333333

title: tutorial
text: Hugging Face datasets also provide predefined validation split. split can attached training task used learners support internal validation, classif.xgboost, early stopping monitoring validation performance. Extract predefined row IDs: Create training task: Create validation task: Create learner: Configure learner use predefined validation task: Train learner: Inspect validation score: Finally, evaluate trained model predefined test split. validation task used learners supporting "validation" property. Learners classif.rpart ignore internal_valid_task, whereas learners classif.xgboost use internal validation early stopping. ## Using tsk() addition HFData sugar function hfdt(), mlr3hf allows Hugging Face datasets created directly using mlr3’s standard tsk() interface providing required dataset parameters. Since tsk("hf", ...) registered like task generator mlr3, integrates directly rest mlr3 ecosystem — example, can used immediately resample(), benchmark(), learner without additional conversion steps.
code: train_ids = hf_data$splits$train valid_ids = hf_data$splits$validation test_ids  = hf_data$splits$test tsk_train = task$clone(deep = TRUE) tsk_train$filter(train_ids) tsk_train$internal_valid_task = valid_ids lrn = lrn("classif.xgboost") lrn$validate = "predefined"  lrn$param_set$set_values(   nrounds = 500,   early_stopping_rounds = 10,   eval_metric = "mlogloss" ) lrn$train(tsk_train) lrn$internal_valid_scores ## $mlogloss ## [1] 13.82791 tsk_test = task$clone(deep = TRUE) tsk_test$filter(test_ids)  pred = lrn$predict(tsk_test)  pred$score(msr("classif.ce")) ## classif.ce  ##  0.6333333 task = tsk("hf", repo_id = "scikit-learn/iris", config = "default", target = "Species",task_type="classif") task ##  ## ── <TaskClassif> (150x6) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ## • Target: Species ## • Properties: multiclass ## • Features (5): ##   • dbl (5): Id, PetalLengthCm, PetalWidthCm, SepalLengthCm, SepalWidthCm ## • Target classes: Iris-setosa (33%), Iris-versicolor (33%), Iris-virginica ## (33%) rr = resample(   task,   lrn("classif.rpart"),   rsmp("holdout") )  rr$aggregate() ## classif.ce  ##          0

title: Hugging Face Dataset Wrapper — HFData
text: R6::R6Class wraps dataset hosted Hugging Face Hub exposes mlr3 compatible data backend / task. Data loaded lazily: download parsing happens fields require access underlying data (e.g. data, nrow, ncol, colnames) accessed first time. Results cached lifetime object. dataset can identified either config (one dataset's predefined configurations, loaded via parquet export) single file_name within repository. Exactly one two must supplied data can retrieved. active bindings read-; attempting assign raises error. See Fields section details one. Note clone(): like every R6 object, HFData objects inherited clone(deep = FALSE) method copying object (deep controls whether nested R6 fields also cloned). re-documented since defined class's source, behaves exactly described R6::R6Class.

title: Hugging Face Dataset Wrapper — HFData
text: repo_id (character(1)) Hugging Face repository id, e.g. "user/dataset". Read-. config (character(1) | NULL) dataset configuration name, specified. Read-. file_name (character(1) | NULL) specific file name within repository, specified. Read-. split (character() | NULL) dataset split (e.g. "train", "test"), specified. Read-. target (character() | NULL) name target column. Read-. desc (list()) repository description/metadata, downloaded Hub first access. Read-. storage (character(1)) Human-readable size storage used whole repository (single file/config). Read-. data (data.frame()) full dataset data frame. Triggers backend creation first access. Read-. nrow (integer(1)) Number rows dataset. Read-. ncol (integer(1)) Number columns dataset. Read-. colnames (character()) Column names dataset. Read-. siblings (character()) File names sibling files repository. Read-. repo_link (character(1)) URL dataset page Hugging Face Hub. Read-. configs (character()) Available dataset configurations, queried datasets-server API. Read-. splits (character()) Available splits selected configuration. Read-. coltypes (character()) Named vector (first) class column. Read-. task_type (character()) One "auto", "classif", "regr". Read-. feature_names (character()) Column names excluding target column. title: Cache a File from a Hugging Face Hub Repository — cache_hfhub

what: Cache a Parquet Export of a Hugging Face Dataset — cache_parquet
title: Cache a Parquet Export of a Hugging Face Dataset — cache_parquet
text: Downloads caches Parquet files dataset hosted Hugging Face Hub, using auto-generated refs/convert/parquet branch. branch contains Parquet conversion dataset Hugging Face maintains automatically, avoids need load dataset via original (often script-based) loading format.

title: Cache a Parquet Export of a Hugging Face Dataset — cache_parquet
code: cache_parquet(   repo_id,   config,   split = NULL,   revision = "refs%2Fconvert%2Fparquet",   ... )

title: Cache a Parquet Export of a Hugging Face Dataset — cache_parquet
text: repo_id Character string. repository ID dataset Hugging Face Hub, form "user_id/repo_name" (e.g. "fancyzhx/amazon_polarity"). config Character string. dataset configuration name. Many datasets expose one configuration, case "default" can usually used. unsure, inspect repository's refs/convert/parquet branch Hub see available configuration folders. split Character string. dataset split cache, "train", "test", "validation". NULL (default), available splits given configuration cached. revision Character string. specific commit hash pin download , instead using latest revision refs/convert/parquet branch. Defaults NULL, resolves recent commit. ... Additional arguments, reserved future use.

title: Cache a Parquet Export of a Hugging Face Dataset — cache_parquet
text: named list one entry per cached split. entry character vector local file paths cached Parquet shard(s) split (single path split one shard, multiple paths sharded across several files).

title: Cache a Parquet Export of a Hugging Face Dataset — cache_parquet
text: Files downloaded refs/convert/parquet branch maintained Hugging Face, dataset's default branch. Large datasets may split across multiple Parquet shards; matching shards requested split downloaded cached.

title: Cache a Parquet Export of a Hugging Face Dataset — cache_parquet
code: if (FALSE) { # interactive() cache_parquet(   repo_id = "scikit-learn/iris",   config  = "default" )  cache_parquet(   repo_id = "fancyzhx/amazon_polarity",   config  = "amazon_polarity",   split   = "train" ) }
